title: Completeness of the Reed–Muller degree test
statement:
Fix a degree bound $d$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function belonging to the Reed–Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(d,n)$, that is, a function of degree at most $d$. Then the $(d+1)$-fold derivative test accepts $f$ with probability exactly $1$:
\[
  \E_{x}\,\E_{h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}}\bigl[\mathbf{1}[\mathrm{GP}((-1)^f,\, d{+}1,\, x,\, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}) = 1]\bigr] = 1,
\]
where $x$ and the direction vectors $h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}$ range uniformly over $\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on {0,1}^n
f lies in the Reed-Muller code RM(d,n), i.e. has degree at most d
replaced:
Every codeword $f \in \mathrm{RM}(d, n)$ is accepted by the degree-$d$ test with
probability $1$.
